description: The presentation: its theme, slides, and settings.

markdownpoint.description: The format version. It is a major and a minor number in quotes, each of at most nine digits and written without a leading zero: "1.0".

id.description: The presentation's id. The .md file has the same id.

save-id.description: The id of the save that last wrote the file while people edited the presentation together. Other saves and other tools leave it unchanged.

theme.description: The key of the presentation's theme. It's the name of the theme's folder in themes. The theme's master sets the slide size and `unit-scale`.

transition.description: The transition from every slide to the next, unless the slide sets its own. Without it, slides cross-dissolve over 0.5 seconds.

soundtrack.description: Music that plays under the whole presentation.

file.description: The audio file's path in the presentation's folder.

loop.description: With `repeat`, it plays again from the start when it ends. Without a loop, it plays once.

fade-in.description: How long it takes to rise linearly from silence each time it starts.

fade-out.description: How long it takes to fall linearly to silence before the file ends each time. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used.

self-playing.description: With it, the presentation plays by itself.

slide-delay.description: How long each slide stays before the next slide. MarkdownPoint sets it to 5 when it makes a presentation self-playing.

click-delay.description: How long the presentation waits before each step that would wait for a click. MarkdownPoint sets it to 2 when it makes a presentation self-playing.

loop.description: With `repeat`, it starts over after the last slide. Without a loop, it stops there.

countdown.description: How long the talk should take in seconds. The presenter's timer counts down from it. Without it, the talk has no set length.

image-style.description: The style generated image objects use when they don't set one: text that isn't blank and has no NUL character, but never `none`. It names no library style. Without it, they have no style.

background-image-style.description: The style generated background images use when they don't set one: text that isn't blank and has no NUL character, but never `none`. It names no library style. Without it, they have no style.

swatches.description: The hex colors the author has saved for this presentation.

date.description: The date the date field shows. It is written YYYY-MM-DD. It must be a real calendar date in year 0001 or later. Without one, the first date field inserted in the app sets it to that day.

locale.description: The presentation's language tag, such as fr-CA. It sets how the date field is written, chart cells are read, and words are split to animate. The default is en-US.

additionalProperties.description: One slide's objects, look, and animation. Its text is in the .md file. A skipped slide has no slide number. The show and every export pass over it, but the PowerPoint export keeps it as a hidden slide. The slide before it goes to the next shown slide with its own transition, and the skipped slide's transition never plays. A link to a skipped slide does nothing.

layout.description: The key of the theme layout the slide uses.

scheme.description: The slide's color scheme. If it's left out or the theme doesn't have it, the slide uses its layout's scheme.

background.description: The slide's own background. It replaces its layout's whole background. A key it leaves out has its default, and an empty background is plain.

fill.description: The color or gradient behind everything.

image.description: The image over the fill. It covers the slide and is cropped as with an image's `scale-mode` `fill`.

file.description: The image's path in the presentation's folder.

crop.description: How far the image is zoomed, and which point stays in view.

exposure.description: How much lighter or darker the image is. It is CSS's `brightness()` of 2 to the power of `exposure` on the sRGB values. 0 leaves it unchanged.

contrast.description: How much more or less contrast the image has. After `exposure`, it is CSS's `contrast()` of 1 + `contrast` on the sRGB values. 0 leaves it unchanged.

saturation.description: How much more or less saturated the image's colors are. After `contrast`, it is CSS's `saturate()` of 1 + `saturation` on the sRGB values. 0 leaves them unchanged.

temperature.description: How much warmer or cooler the image's colors are. After `saturation`, red is multiplied by 1 + `temperature` ÷ 4 and blue by 1 − `temperature` ÷ 4. 0 leaves them unchanged.

grayscale.description: How far the colors fade to gray. After `temperature`, it is CSS's `grayscale()` of `grayscale` on the sRGB values. 0 leaves them unchanged.

drop-shadow.description: A drop shadow behind the image.

prompt.description: The prompt for a generated background image. It is any text without a NUL character.

image-style.description: The style of a generated background image: text that isn't blank and has no NUL character, or `none` for no style. It names no library style. The default is `background-image-style`.

transparent-background.description: Whether a generated background image is made with a transparent background.

restyle.description: A style or an edit that the image model applies to the image as it was first made. It names no library style. Until a generation with an `original` applies it, the image shows its `file` as it is.

generation.description: Which image generation record made the background image. For a restyle, it also names the image the restyle was applied to.

skipped.description: Whether the slide is skipped. A skipped slide stays in the presentation and has no number. The show and every export pass over it, but the PowerPoint export keeps it as a hidden slide.

transition.description: The transition from this slide to the next.

The camera's motion blur. The 3D layer blurs along its motion while the shutter is open. Nothing else is blurred. Only exported movies and the Agent's renders show it. A frame is a sixtieth of a second, a movie's frame. The Agent's renders use the same frame at any `sampleRate`.

shutter.description: How long the shutter stays open in frames. At 0, there is no blur. The default is 0.5. It can be animated.

shutter-position.description: Where the frame's moment falls in the shutter's opening: at its start, its center, or its end. The default is center.

samples.description: How many moments the 3D layer is drawn at while the shutter is open. The drawings are then averaged. Cinema 4D's Sub-Frame Motion Blur Samples work the same way. The default is 32.

anyOf.description: The slide's render settings, kept on its camera beside motion blur: a fast estimate of light bouncing between surfaces, and of the World's light blocked where surfaces meet. In Cinema 4D's Render Settings, they are Global Illumination and Ambient Occlusion. The effects show wherever the 3D layer shows. Only surfaces in view bounce light. A shadow catcher or a floor bounces none. An override replaces the whole record.

global-illumination.description: Whether lit surfaces bounce their light onto what is near them. The default is false.

ambient-occlusion.description: Whether the World's light darkens where surfaces close in on each other. A shadow catcher or a floor then also darkens where an object rests on it. The default is false.

distance.description: How far bounced light and shading reach from a surface. The default is 400.

anyOf.description: The camera's drift. Its offset is in canvas units along the slide's 3D axes. After animation, parenting, and constraints place the camera, the offset is added to its position and its point of interest. A parent's rotation and scale don't change it. The drift runs on the slide's own clock. That clock starts when the slide's transition in begins. It runs on through the slide's steps, waits, and transition out. While t is less than `duration`, the added offset at t seconds on that clock is `offset` × (1 − t ÷ `duration`)². The offset decreases to zero at `duration` and stays zero afterward. Stills and the editor show the camera without its drift. A slide has no drift when a scroll transition enters or leaves it.

offset.description: Where the camera starts: an {x, y, z} offset from its set position.

duration.description: How many seconds after the slide begins to appear the camera comes to rest.

anyOf.description: A constraint that moves the slide's camera with an object. Cinema 4D's Position constraint works the same way. Only the camera can have it. With a spring, the camera follows on a spring with that response and damping ratio. It trails a sudden move, catches up, and settles as the object stops. If the spring is still moving 10 seconds after what it follows has stopped, the camera halts where it got to. It stops short of its target. It stays there until a click moves what it follows again. Every key except `id`, `type`, and `target` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as follow. It is unique among the camera's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.follow.strength`.

target.description: The id of the model or light the camera follows.

target-node.description: The name of a node in the target's model, such as ball. The camera follows the node as the model's Action moves it. Without it, the camera follows the target's origin.

axes.description: A list of one or more of the 3D space's axes the camera follows on, such as `["x"]`. Each axis is listed once. The axes can be in any order. Without it, the camera follows on all three.

relative-to-target.description: Whether the camera follows the target at an offset: its own offset from the slide's center at z 0, added to the target's point. With false, it is at the target's point. The default is true.

strength.description: How far the camera moves to the point it follows: 0 is not at all and 1 is fully. The default is 1. It can be animated.

spring.description: The spring the camera follows on. It has the `damping-ratio` and `response` of a keyframe's `spring` interpolation. Without it, the camera follows exactly.

damping-ratio.description: How strongly the spring is damped. At 1, it is critically damped. Less damping swings further.

response.description: The spring's natural period. A shorter response catches up sooner.

overrides.description: Changes by id to what the slide inherits from its layout and master. They're kept even if they match what's inherited. An object set to `null` is removed. The camera and the World can't be removed.

poster.description: a file path in the presentation's folder

objects.description: The slide's objects, back to front, a tilted group's members by depth. Its own are written out, and an inherited one is listed by its id. An inherited one the list doesn't name is behind them all. An id listed twice is refused, and one the slide doesn't inherit is ignored with a warning.

initial.description: Each animated parameter's value until a step animates it, or for the whole slide when none does. Its key is "object.parameter", such as "card.opacity". A `null` clears the whole parameter.

slides.description: The slides by id. The .md file has their order and text.

additionalProperties.description: A reusable animated scene that slides show as instances. A composition can't contain itself, directly or through another. Its canvas is as large as fits in the instance's frame and is centered there. Then it turns and scales with the instance about the instance's anchor point. The composition's objects are in their own group at the instance's position. That group counts toward how deep groups nest. A composition can contain only what a group can: nothing 3D, no audio object, and no web video. Like a group, an instance fades and blurs as one picture and fades each branch on its own where a group would. A mask at the composition's root clips nothing. An instance's `visible: false` hides all its objects. A click on any of its objects follows its `link`, unless that object has a link of its own.

name.description: The composition's name: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks. The default is the composition's id with spaces for its hyphens and a capital first letter.

preview-scheme.description: The color scheme its own canvas shows while it's edited and when it's rendered on its own. Light is the default and stands in for a scheme the theme lacks. Each instance uses its slide's scheme.

items.description: One control a composition offers its instances. Its default matches its type: a number, true or false, a color, one of its options' ids, or a file path for a media control. The objects a media control binds all have the same type. Where they don't, the control reads with an `invalid-binding` warning. Its default and its values are files of that type.

id.description: The id that names the control in a binding, an instance's value, and a marker. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks. Two controls can have the same name.

id.description: The id that names the control in a binding, an instance's value, and a marker. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks. Two controls can have the same name.

default.description: The value used when an instance doesn't set one. A number control's default is from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

min.description: A number control's smallest value, below its max.

max.description: A number control's largest value, above its min.

id.description: The id that names the control in a binding, an instance's value, and a marker. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks. Two controls can have the same name.

default.description: The value used when an instance doesn't set one. A number control's default is from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

id.description: The id that names the control in a binding, an instance's value, and a marker. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks. Two controls can have the same name.

default.description: The value used when an instance doesn't set one. A number control's default is from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

id.description: The id that names the control in a binding, an instance's value, and a marker. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks. Two controls can have the same name.

default.description: The value used when an instance doesn't set one. A number control's default is from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

items.description: One option of a choice control. The options are in the order its pop-up shows them.

id.description: The id that names the option in the control's default, an instance's value, and the value of a key the choice sets. It's unique among the control's options.

name.description: The words the author sees: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters, no white space at either end, and no comma: ",", "，", or "、".

options.description: A choice control's one or more options in the order its pop-up shows them. Its default is one of their ids.

id.description: The id that names the control in a binding, an instance's value, and a marker. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks. Two controls can have the same name.

default.description: The value used when an instance doesn't set one. A number control's default is from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

controls.description: The controls each instance can set in the order they're shown.

objects.description: Its objects, back to front, a tilted group's members by depth. It can't contain a model, light, shadow catcher, floor, camera, World, audio object, web video, or text with a `model`.

initial.description: Each animated parameter's value until a step animates it, or for the whole composition when none does. Its key is "object.parameter". A `null` clears the whole parameter.

steps.description: Its steps, grouped into clicks as a slide's are. The clicks play back to back. They have no cues and no `loop`. With every pass counted, they last at most 4,294,967,296 seconds.

compositions.description: Reusable animated scenes by id. Slides show them as instances.

additionalProperties.description: A comment pinned to a slide or a composition. It can have replies. Its id is unique among the presentation's comments.

slide.description: The id of the slide it is pinned to. It can name a slide that is no longer there.

composition.description: The id of the composition it is pinned to. It can name a composition that is no longer there.

created.description: When it was written: a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as 2026-10-16T09:30:00.000Z.

text.description: What it says. It isn't blank and has no control characters except line breaks and tabs. Its line breaks are line feeds. A carriage return, alone or before a line feed, is read as a line feed.

position.description: Where it is pinned: {x, y} in canvas units on the slide or composition. When the slide size changes, it moves with the slide's objects.

resolved.description: Whether the comment is resolved. The default is false.

additionalProperties.description: One reply to a comment. Its id is unique among the comment's replies.

created.description: When it was written: a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as 2026-10-16T09:30:00.000Z.

text.description: What it says. It isn't blank and has no control characters except line breaks and tabs. Its line breaks are line feeds. A carriage return, alone or before a line feed, is read as a line feed.

replies.description: The replies by id. They are read by their `created` time, then by their id. Each has an author, a created time, and text.

comments.description: Comments by id. They are read by their `created` time, then by their id. Each one is pinned to a slide or a composition.

anchor-point.description: The point an object turns and scales about. A group also tilts about it. It is in fractions of the box the object is drawn at: its frame; a growing text box's box at the size of its words; a table's box at its columns' widths and its rows' heights; or a group's box. Without one, an object turns and scales about its center. A text box that grows turns and scales about the point its text grows from. Leaving it out is the only way to the default.

x.description: How far across the box in fractions of its width.

y.description: How far down the box in fractions of its height.

area-size.description: An area light's size along its own axes in canvas units. In Redshift's Area Light, they are Size X and Size Y.

x.description: Its width, along its own x.

y.description: Its height, along its own y.

auto-layout.description: How a group places its members one after another. The defaults are direction vertical, gap 0, align start, and reference-point start. Members are placed in their order in the `objects` list. Members whose `visible` is false, members with `ignore-auto-layout`, and lines attached to an object are skipped. A step or an initial value that hides or shows a member doesn't move the others. The run goes down or across in the group's rotation, and no member turns with it. A member's repeater copies take no room in it. Any other line takes the box of its two ends, and a member group the box its own members take.

direction.description: Whether the members run down or across.

gap.description: The space between one member and the next.

align.description: How the members line up across the layout's direction.

reference-point.description: Which point of the run stays at the group's frame as the members grow or shrink: its start, center, or end along the layout's direction.

back.description: How far `anticipate`, `overshoot`, or `anticipate-overshoot` pulls back or swings past. Robert Penner's back curves and Blender's Back use it the same way. The default is 1.70158.

color.description: a color role or a hex color

comment-author.description: Who wrote a comment. Its `id` has one of three forms. For a computer's user, it is `local:` followed by a lowercase UUID. For a Dropbox user, it is `dropbox:` followed by the Dropbox account id as Dropbox's API spells it. That account id is `dbid:` followed by one or more of A to Z, a to z, 0 to 9, `_`, and `-`. For a Microsoft account user, it is `microsoft:` followed by the account's Microsoft Graph id in lowercase. That id is a UUID for a work or school account and 16 hexadecimal digits for a personal account.

id.description: Who wrote it, if known. It is in one of the record's three forms.

name.description: The name the comment shows for the author. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks.

propertyNames.description: a key or a number part of a record, such as "tilt.x"

anyOf.description: A constraint that turns a model, or one of its nodes, toward a target. Cinema 4D's Aim constraint works the same way. Every key except `id`, `type`, and `target` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as look. It is unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.look.strength`.

node.description: The name of the model's node that turns, such as Head. Without it, the whole model turns.

target.description: The id of the model or light whose origin it turns toward. With `camera`, it turns toward the camera.

axis.description: The axis of the model or node that points at the target in its GLB's axes. In those axes, y is up, and a model faces along +z. The default is z.

strength.description: How far it turns toward the target: 0 is not at all and 1 is fully. It applies to the result of the constraints before it. The default is 1. It can be animated.

anyOf.description: A constraint that keeps a model's volume as the model scales along its own axes. The volume is measured at the model's `scale` as the object sets it, before any `initial` value or step. An axis it scales stops at a 3D scale's most, 1 × 10¹⁸ either way, and an axis at 0 stays at 0. Every key except `id` and `type` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as squash. It is unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.squash.strength`.

mode.description: When the volume is kept. With `strict`, it always is. With `uniform`, it is kept while the model scales evenly. With `single-axis`, it is kept while only the free axis scales. The default is strict.

free-axis.description: The axis the constraint leaves as it is. It scales the other two to keep the volume. The default is y.

volume.description: The volume to keep. It is a multiple of the model's volume at its `scale`. The default is 1. At 0.4, the model is squeezed to 40% of its volume. The model's size is its `scale`, not this.

strength.description: How strongly it keeps the volume: 0 is not at all and 1 is fully. The default is 1. It can be animated.

crop.description: An image's or a video's zoom inside its frame, and the point that stays in view. The defaults are scale 1 and focal-point 0.5, 0.5.

scale.description: How far it is zoomed. At 1, an image fits its frame as its `scale-mode` sets, and a background covers the slide. Above 1, it is zoomed in. Below 1, it is zoomed out.

focal-point.description: The point that stays in view: {x, y}. Each is a fraction of the image, across and down.

anyOf.description: A drop shadow. Its keys work like those of Photoshop's Drop Shadow. First, what the object paints grows solid by size × spread. Then it is blurred by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. The size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far it reaches in canvas units.

spread.description: The fraction of the size that is solid. The rest of the size is blurred. At 1, the shadow is solid all the way out. Photoshop's Spread works the same way. The default is 0.

offset.description: How far it falls: {x, y} across and down in the object's own axes. It turns and scales with the object and its groups. A flip doesn't mirror it. A background's offset is in the slide's axes.

color.description: Its color: a color role, or a hex color written #RGB or #RRGGBB. A role's alpha is ignored. The shadow's opacity is set by `opacity` alone.

enter.description: Text that enters piece by piece. `based-on` sets whether a piece is a paragraph, a word, or a character. The defaults are interpolation linear, fade 1, order forward, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 1. With delivery `by-paragraph`, it works as PowerPoint's By Paragraph.

based-on.description: What counts as one piece. With `character-and-space`, each space is a piece too. After Effects' Characters is `character-and-space`, and its Characters Excluding Spaces is `character`.

delivery.description: `by-paragraph`: each paragraph enters on the step whose paragraph cue names it. It needs based-on `paragraph` and no seed. Order, spread, pause, and progress must be at their defaults.

duration.description: How long each paragraph takes to enter in seconds. With interpolation hold, it is still required but isn't used. A step that has only paragraphs' cues lasts as long as they take.

from.description: How each piece looks as it starts to enter: opacity, offset, scale, rotation, and blur.

offset.description: How far it starts from where it rests: {x, y} across and down in ems of the piece's own font size. On a path, x is along the path, and y is down from it as its letters stand on it.

scale.description: Its scale. At 1, it is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is: its radius in ems of the piece's own font size.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves into place: gradually, or at once with hold. A text's spring has no `response`, and its elastic has no `period`.

fade.description: The fraction of each piece's entrance its fade lasts. The fade starts with the move and follows the piece's interpolation.

order.description: The order the pieces enter in. With a seed, it must be `random`.

seed.description: The seed for a random order: the same seed gives the same order. The default is 0.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for. In forward, backward, or random order, this many pieces move at once.

pause.description: How many intervals the text waits between turns. `enter` says how they count.

progress.description: How far the text has entered. It is animated by steps. It isn't animated when the entrance has a `delivery`.

exit.description: Text that exits piece by piece. Its pieces are counted and timed the same way as an entrance's pieces. The defaults are interpolation linear, fade 1, order forward, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 0.

based-on.description: What counts as one piece. With `character-and-space`, each space is a piece too. After Effects' Characters is `character-and-space`, and its Characters Excluding Spaces is `character`.

to.description: How each piece looks as it finishes exiting: opacity, offset, scale, rotation, and blur.

offset.description: How far it ends from where it rests: {x, y} across and down in ems of the piece's own font size. On a path, x is along the path, and y is down from it as its letters stand on it.

scale.description: Its scale. At 1, it is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is: its radius in ems of the piece's own font size.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves out of place: gradually, or at once with hold. A text's spring has no `response`, and its elastic has no `period`.

fade.description: The fraction of each piece's exit its fade lasts. The fade ends with the move and follows the piece's interpolation.

order.description: The order the pieces exit in. With a seed, it must be `random`.

seed.description: The seed for a random order: the same seed gives the same order. The default is 0.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for. In forward, backward, or random order, this many pieces move at once.

pause.description: How many intervals the text waits between turns. `enter` says how they count.

progress.description: How far the text has exited. It is animated by steps.

flat-scale.description: A flat object's scale along its own axes. The object scales about its `anchor-point`. Text breaks into lines first, then stretches with the scale.

floor-position.description: A floor's height in the 3D space. A floor is level and goes on without end. So a floor's position has only y. Like a shadow catcher, a floor shows only the shadows cast on it and hides the 3D objects behind it. Without a position, the floor is at the slide's bottom edge.

y.description: How far up from the slide's bottom edge in canvas units.

frame.description: An object's position and size in canvas units from the top left of its slide or composition. A table's, an audio object's, and a group's frame has only x and y: their contents, an icon, or members give them their size. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom. A group has a frame only with `auto-layout`. Its frame is the position of the auto layout's run: the box its members' frames make, unturned and unscaled, placed one after another. The `reference-point` of the group's auto layout says which point of the run that is: the top left in the group's rotation, or the center or end along the layout's direction.

x.description: How far across the left edge is. When a text box's width grows, it is the point the text is aligned to. For a group, it is the point its auto layout's `reference-point` names.

y.description: How far down the top edge is. When a text box's height grows, its default `anchor-point` is on its top edge. For a group, it is the point its auto layout's `reference-point` names.

generation.description: How a generated or restyled image was made.

id.description: The id of the image generation record that made the image. It is the lowercase UUID in the record's file name, `generated/<id>.json`.

original.description: The image a restyle was applied to. It is present only when the record is for a restyle.

file.description: Its file's path in the presentation's folder. The path ends in an image's extension.

generation.description: How it was made, if it was generated. Without it, the image wasn't generated.

id.description: The id of its image generation record. It is the lowercase UUID in the record's file name, `generated/<id>.json`.

angle.description: A linear gradient's direction in degrees clockwise from up.

line.description: Where a linear gradient's line is in the box the object is drawn at. It turns about its middle by `angle`. By default it crosses the box it spans through its center. It is the same in CSS.

x.description: The x of its middle in fractions of the box's width. 0 is the left edge, and 1 is the right edge.

y.description: The y of its middle in fractions of the box's height. 0 is the top edge, and 1 is the bottom edge.

length.description: Its length in fractions of the box's diagonal.

stops.description: The gradient's two or more colors and their positions.

center.description: The center of a radial gradient: {x, y}.

x.description: Its x in fractions of the box's width. 0 is the left edge, and 1 is the right edge.

y.description: Its y in fractions of the box's height. 0 is the top edge, and 1 is the bottom edge.

shape.description: With `circle`, a radial gradient is round in any box. Without it, it is an ellipse.

stops.description: The gradient's two or more colors and their positions.

image-style-not-none.description: nonempty text without NUL characters, not "none"

image-style-or-none.description: nonempty text without NUL characters, or "none"

propertyNames.description: an object's id, a dot, and a parameter, such as "card.opacity"

line-end.description: A line end attached to an object.

object.description: The id of the object it attaches to on the same slide or composition.

side.description: Which side of the object's frame it attaches to. The sides turn with the object's `rotation`, and a flip doesn't change them. With `auto`, it attaches to the side that faces the other end.

model-node-name.description: the name of one of the model's nodes

nonblank-line.description: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks

opaque-color.description: a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000"

point-frame.description: An object's position and size in canvas units from the top left of its slide or composition. A table's, an audio object's, and a group's frame has only x and y: their contents, an icon, or members give them their size. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom. A group has a frame only with `auto-layout`. Its frame is the position of the auto layout's run: the box its members' frames make, unturned and unscaled, placed one after another. The `reference-point` of the group's auto layout says which point of the run that is: the top left in the group's rotation, or the center or end along the layout's direction.

x.description: How far across the left edge is. When a text box's width grows, it is the point the text is aligned to. For a group, it is the point its auto layout's `reference-point` names.

y.description: How far down the top edge is. When a text box's height grows, its default `anchor-point` is on its top edge. For a group, it is the point its auto layout's `reference-point` names.

repeater.description: Copies of the object. Each is moved, turned, scaled, and delayed a little more than the one before. The original stays as written. The defaults are 1 for `scale` and `end-opacity`, the center for `anchor-point`, and 0 for the other optional numbers.

copies.description: How many copies there are. The original counts as one.

position.description: The move from each copy to the next: {x, y} across and down. It is measured in the turned and scaled axes of the copy before.

rotation.description: How far each copy is turned clockwise from the one before.

scale.description: How much each copy is scaled from the one before. At 1, each copy is the same size as the one before.

anchor-point.description: The point `rotation` and `scale` turn and scale the copies about: {x, y}. Each is a fraction of the box the object is drawn at, across and down. A group's is the group's box.

stagger.description: How much later each copy plays the object's animation than the one before. A copy can play it up to (copies − 1) × `stagger` + `stagger-randomness` later.

end-opacity.description: The last copy's opacity. It is a fraction of the object's opacity. The copies between fade toward it evenly. After Effects' End Opacity works the same way with a Start Opacity of 100%.

position-randomness.description: The farthest each copy moves in a random direction.

rotation-randomness.description: The farthest each copy turns either way at random about its own center. Motion's Replicator Angle Randomness works the same way.

scale-randomness.description: The most each copy grows or shrinks at random about its own center. It is a fraction of its size.

stagger-randomness.description: The most extra time each copy waits at random.

seed.description: The random seed: the same seed gives the same copies. Motion's Random Seed works the same way.

restyle.description: A style or an edit that the image model applies to the image as it was first made: a copy of a library style's `name`, `prompt` and `transparent-background`, or the author's own. It names no library style. Until a generation with an `original` applies it, the image shows its `file` as it is.

name.description: The style's name: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks.

prompt.description: How the style changes an image: an edit prompt. It isn't blank.

transparent-background.description: Whether images in the style have transparent backgrounds.

space-euler.description: A 3D object's rotation about its origin, in its space's axes: its parent's for a parented object, otherwise x right, y up, and z toward the viewer. It is in degrees, or a quaternion in quaternion mode. An object's own rotation in degrees needs x, y, and z. In degrees, it turns in Cinema 4D's HPB order: by the heading about y, then by the pitch about its own x, then by the bank about its own z. In three.js, this is Euler order YXZ. A positive z turns it counterclockwise on the slide, a positive x tilts its top toward the viewer, and a positive y brings its left side forward. A quaternion is glTF's with w first. A Blender quaternion (w, x, y, z) exported to glTF with +Y up is (w, x, z, −y) here. A quaternion's parts are read to six decimal places, and its length doesn't change the rotation. Between two quaternion keyframes, the object turns the shorter way round.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z.

space-position.description: A point in the 3D space in canvas units. The x axis runs right from the slide's left edge, the y axis runs up from its bottom edge, and the z axis runs toward the viewer. The slide is at z 0. The axes are right-handed. glTF and three.js use the same axes. After Effects' y and z axes run the other way. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

space-quaternion.description: A 3D object's rotation about its origin, in its space's axes: its parent's for a parented object, otherwise x right, y up, and z toward the viewer. It is in degrees, or a quaternion in quaternion mode. An object's own rotation in degrees needs x, y, and z. In degrees, it turns in Cinema 4D's HPB order: by the heading about y, then by the pitch about its own x, then by the bank about its own z. In three.js, this is Euler order YXZ. A positive z turns it counterclockwise on the slide, a positive x tilts its top toward the viewer, and a positive y brings its left side forward. A quaternion is glTF's with w first. A Blender quaternion (w, x, y, z) exported to glTF with +Y up is (w, x, z, −y) here. A quaternion's parts are read to six decimal places, and its length doesn't change the rotation. Between two quaternion keyframes, the object turns the shorter way round.

w.description: A quaternion's w. It is used in quaternion mode only.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z.

space-scale.description: A 3D object's scale along its own axes, about its origin. A negative scale mirrors the object along that axis. Objects parented to a light are scaled with it. An area light's surface is scaled too. A move between two scales of one sign stops at 0. A wave can take a scale past 0.

items.description: One step: the keyframes and cues that a click or the previous step sets off. Its times and the times of its keyframes and cues are in seconds. They are rounded to six decimal places. Its `with-previous` and `after-previous` start work as PowerPoint's With Previous and After Previous. On the first step, either starts it as the slide's transition ends. A Scroll into the slide plays its first click with the move, whatever its start. A cue that starts a sound, a video, or a clip counts at its own time alone. The step doesn't wait for what it starts to play through. The Animate tab's Add Action gives a clip's step the Action's length as its `min-duration`.

id.description: The step's id, unique on its slide or composition.

name.description: The step's name: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks.

start.description: When the step starts. `on-click` starts it on a click of its own and is the default. `with-previous` starts it with the previous step. `after-previous` starts it after that step ends.

min-duration.description: The least time the step lasts in seconds. A later keyframe, cue, entering paragraph, or repeated copy makes it longer. Without it, or at 0, the step lasts as long as what is in it.

repeat-count.description: How many times the step plays before it completes. Without it, the step plays once. The step plays only as many times as fit in 4,294,967,296 seconds. A larger count causes a warning.

loop.description: With `repeat`, the step loops from `loop-start` to its end while it waits for a click. Without it, the step plays once.

loop-start.description: The seconds into the step where `loop` starts. Without it, the loop starts at 0. At or past the later of its `min-duration` and its last keyframe or cue, it causes a warning and doesn't loop.

propertyNames.description: an object's id, a dot, and a parameter, such as "card.opacity"

additionalProperties.description: One parameter's animation in a step: its keyframes and what happens after the last one. A position can also be keyed as one point. `frame.position` and `translation` have {x, y}, and `position` has {x, y, z}. Each of their keyframes has every part. A step keys a position either as a point or by its parts, not both. A step that keys both is read with a warning, and the point plays. An initial value sets each part on its own.

One keyframe: a value a parameter reaches at a time. Its id is unique in its step among its keyframes and cues. Two keyframes of one parameter at one time are read with a warning, and the one with the later id plays. A `begin` at or before the previous keyframe is ignored. On the first keyframe, a `begin` of 0 is ignored. A `discrete` key and interpolation `hold` have no move. A `begin` on either is ignored. A keyframe whose value is `null` clears the whole parameter at its time. The parameter's text style or default then shows. It can't clear a part of a key, a point, `visible`, `rotation`, `scale`, a constraint's strength, `shape-type`, `icon`, or `geometry`. A `null` on a key its object can't be read without, such as a shadow catcher's `width` or a point light's `intensity`, causes an `ignored-animation-value` warning and is ignored. A slide's or a composition's `initial` takes `null` by the same rules. An `exponential-scale` move works as After Effects' Exponential Scale.

begin.description: When the keyframe's move begins. It is in seconds into the step. It must come before `time`. Without it, the move begins at the previous keyframe, or at 0 for the first keyframe.

time.description: When the parameter reaches the value. It is in seconds into the step.

value.description: The value. It is written as the parameter is. It can be `null` to clear the whole parameter. It is the parameter's own value, not a change from the object's rest.

anyOf.description: An interpolation with its settings: how far `anticipate`, `overshoot`, or `anticipate-overshoot` pulls back or swings past, an elastic's swing, a bounce's bounciness, a spring's damping ratio, or a cubic Bézier's two handles. The handles' keys are named the way CSS's cubic-bezier() names its four numbers. A named curve with no settings is written as just its name. A cubic Bézier that is the same as a named curve is written as that named curve's name too.

amplitude.description: The size of an elastic's swing in multiples of the move. The default is 1.

period.description: How long one swing of an elastic lasts. The default is 0.3 of the length of the move.

bounciness.description: A bounce's rebound speed in fractions of its landing speed. At 0, it lands dead. At 1, it rebounds to its height each time. The default 0.5 is Blender's Bounce.

damping-ratio.description: How strongly a spring is damped. At 1, it doesn't swing past its keyframe. Less damping swings further.

response.description: The spring's natural period. A shorter one springs faster. Without it, the spring settles by the end of the move.

x1.description: The time of a cubic Bézier's first handle in fractions of the move.

y1.description: The value of a cubic Bézier's first handle in fractions of the change. It can be below 0 or above 1. The move can then go past an end. It stops at the end of the parameter's range.

x2.description: The time of a cubic Bézier's second handle in fractions of the move.

y2.description: The value of a cubic Bézier's second handle in fractions of the change. It can be below 0 or above 1. The move can then go past an end. It stops at the end of the parameter's range.

interpolation.description: How the value reaches the keyframe: gradually, or at once with hold. It is a named curve, a named curve with its settings, a cubic Bézier, or a spring. The default is linear.

interrupted.description: The longer move this keyframe interrupts. Up to the keyframe's time, the motion follows that move toward its `value`. Then the parameter has the keyframe's own `value`.

time.description: When the move would have reached `value`. It is in seconds into the step and at or after the keyframe's time. It doesn't make the step longer.

motion-path.description: A curved motion path for the keyframe's move. Only a point keyframe can have it.

geometry.description: The path: SVG path data from the move's start at 0 0 to its end at 1 0. It is one open contour of 2 to 8,192 points. It has at most 2,097,152 characters.

orient.description: Whether the object turns to face along the path. The default is false.

exponential-scale.description: Whether a scale move changes by a steady ratio. A zoom then looks even. Its pace is even from or to 0, or across it. It applies only to `scale`, `scale.x`, `scale.y`, `scale.z`, and `crop.scale`.

oscillate.description: A wave added to the value from this keyframe to the next, or to the step's end. On a looping curve, the wave plays again each time around.

amplitude.description: How far the value swings either way in the parameter's own unit. The value stops at the end of the parameter's range.

frequency.description: How many full cycles each second. A noise wave wanders at that rate. After Effects' wiggle() frequency works the same way.

phase.description: Where in its cycle the wave starts. A cycle is 360 degrees. The default is 0.

wave-shape.description: The wave's shape. With a seed, it must be `noise`. The default is sine.

seed.description: The noise seed. A seed picks one wave. The default is 0. Motion's Random Seed works the same way.

keyframes.description: The keyframes by id, one or more. They are read by their time, then by their id.

loop.description: How it loops after its last keyframe until the step ends. With `repeat`, it replays from `loop-keyframe` to the last. With `ping-pong`, it plays that back and forth. Without it, it plays once.

loop-keyframe.description: The id of the keyframe the loop starts at. If the keyframe has a `begin`, the loop begins with its move. If it names no keyframe of the curve, the first is used.

curves.description: The step's animation. Each curve is under an "object.parameter" key such as card.opacity.

additionalProperties.description: An event at a set time in a step. Its id is unique in its step among its keyframes and cues. A clip plays an Action of the GLB `file` of a model or a 3D text. Cinema 4D's Motion Clip works the same way. A text built from an `extrusion` has no Actions. A clip on it plays nothing and causes a warning.

time.description: When it happens. It is in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on: for a clip, a model, or a 3D text.

paragraph.description: The id of the paragraph that appears: the `<!-- id: … -->` ending its last line or alone on the next. A list item's ends its first paragraph. A reader warns when no paragraph of the text has the id.

time.description: When it happens. It is in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on: for a clip, a model, or a 3D text.

time.description: When it happens. It is in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on: for a clip, a model, or a 3D text.

action.description: The name of the Action that a clip plays. An unnamed Action is named Animation and its number in the file, as in `Animation 1` for the first.

loop.description: With `repeat`, the Action plays again from the start of its `clip-trim` each time it ends. Without it, it plays once, even an Action made to repeat. A model's `stride` times it by travel instead.

clip-trim.description: The part of the Action that plays: a start and an end in seconds into the Action.

stride.description: How far the model travels per cycle of its Action in the GLB's meters. The Action's timing then follows the model's travel. It doesn't apply to a 3D text's clip.

blend-in.description: How long the clip takes to blend in fully over the model's current motion. Without it, the clip is fully blended in from its start.

clip-scale.description: How much longer a clip's Action plays than its file says. 2 is half speed, and 0.5 is double. Maya's Clip Scale works the same way. The default is 1. It isn't used by a model's clip with a `stride`.

cues.description: Events at set times in the step by id. They are read by their time, then by their id. Each shows a paragraph, starts an audio object, a video, or a web video, or plays a clip.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

position.description: Where the color is along the gradient from 0 to 1. A stop is never before the previous one.

tail.description: The tip of a speech bubble's tail.

x.description: How far across the frame in fractions of its width.

y.description: How far down the frame in fractions of its height.

anyOf.description: A text's drop shadow. Its keys work like those of Photoshop's Drop Shadow. Its lengths are in ems of the text's font size. First, the text's letters and outline grow solid by size × spread. Then it is blurred by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. The size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far the shadow reaches beyond the text's letters and outline. Photoshop's Size works the same way.

spread.description: The fraction of the size that is solid. The rest of the size is blurred. At 1, the shadow is solid all the way out. Photoshop's Spread works the same way. The default is 0.

offset.description: How far the shadow falls: {x, y} across and down in the text's own axes. It turns and scales with the text and its groups.

color.description: Its color: a color role, or a hex color written #RGB or #RRGGBB. A role's alpha is ignored. The shadow's opacity is set by `opacity` alone.

text-frame.description: An object's position and size in canvas units from the top left of its slide or composition. A table's, an audio object's, and a group's frame has only x and y: their contents, an icon, or members give them their size. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom. A group has a frame only with `auto-layout`. Its frame is the position of the auto layout's run: the box its members' frames make, unturned and unscaled, placed one after another. The `reference-point` of the group's auto layout says which point of the run that is: the top left in the group's rotation, or the center or end along the layout's direction.

x.description: How far across the left edge is. When a text box's width grows, it is the point the text is aligned to. For a group, it is the point its auto layout's `reference-point` names.

y.description: How far down the top edge is. When a text box's height grows, its default `anchor-point` is on its top edge. For a group, it is the point its auto layout's `reference-point` names.

text-model.description: A text's 3D model. Its `type` is `extrusion` or `file`. With `extrusion`, MarkdownPoint builds the words' letters into a model. A text on a path can't have an extrusion. Its extrusion is left out as the file is read, and the warning `extrusion-with-text-path` says so. Its words draw flat. Each length is in ems of the text's size. The default depth is 0.2, and the default bevel is 0.02. With `file`, the model is a GLB that a program built, and `built-from` is the fingerprint of what it was built from: the words, the values of the fields they show, the presentation's `locale`, and the text's style and layout. Once any of them changes, the words draw flat until the model is built again. One unit of the model is one em of the text's size. Its origin is on the first line's baseline at the left of the text's column. For words on a path, its origin is the frame's top left. That is the path's 0 0, and the model's y points up from it. The model moves, turns, and scales with the text's frame. Its `z` sets how far it is in front of the slide. The text is never in a group or a composition. Its depth scales by the square root of the text's x scale times its y scale. A step's clips play the Actions of a GLB `file` the same way they play a model's. An extrusion has no Actions. Its letters are matte and lit only by the slide's lights and its World. With no light and the World's intensity at 0, its default, they draw black.

depth.description: How far the letters are extruded in ems. The bevels on the front and the back add `bevel` each. The letters' fronts are then `depth` + 2 × `bevel` from the slide.

bevel.description: How far the letters' edges are rounded in ems. At 0, they are sharp.

file.description: The path in the presentation's folder of the GLB a program built from the words.

built-from.description: The fingerprint of what the GLB was built from. The reference gives the rule. A reader that doesn't know the rule treats the model as out of sync.

tilt.description: How far a group tilts in depth about axes through its anchor point in the slide's plane. It is in degrees.

x.description: It turns about the horizontal axis. With a positive x, its top turns away from the viewer. CSS's `rotateX()` turns the same way. A 3D object's `rotation.x` turns the other way.

y.description: It turns about the vertical axis. With a positive y, its left side comes forward. The group's rotation comes first, then the y turn, then the x turn.

time-trim.description: The part of a video or audio file, or of a clip's Action, that plays.

start.description: Where it starts in seconds into the file or the Action. The default is 0.

end.description: Where it ends in seconds into the file or the Action. It must come after start. Without it, the file or the Action plays to its end.

transition.description: A slide transition. `cross-dissolve` crossfades to the next slide. `carry-over` moves each object with the same id on both slides. `push` moves both slides along its direction, `move-in` brings the next slide in over this one, and `reveal` moves this one off the next. `scroll` makes both slides one strip the view travels across. This slide stays as it was left, and the next slide's first click plays with the move. `wipe` uncovers the next slide behind a traveling edge. `zoom` grows the next slide in from the middle. `fade-through-color` fades this slide out to the color and the next one in from it. The defaults are interpolation ease-in-out, match object, direction left, color #000000, and delay 0.

start.description: When it starts: on a click, or by itself after the slide's last step. The default is `on-click`. Keynote's Start Transition Automatically works the same way.

delay.description: How long a transition that starts by itself waits after the slide's last step ends. It goes only beside `start: automatically`. Keynote's Delay works the same way.

duration.description: How long it takes. It's left out when the type is `none`.

delay.description: How long a transition that starts by itself waits after the slide's last step ends. It goes only beside `start: automatically`. Keynote's Delay works the same way.

duration.description: How long it takes. It's left out when the type is `none`.

interpolation.description: How the transition speeds up and slows down. Only `carry-over` and `scroll` have it.

match.description: What `carry-over` matches between two texts: objects, words, or characters. Keynote's Magic Move matches them the same way.

start.description: When it starts: on a click, or by itself after the slide's last step. The default is `on-click`. Keynote's Start Transition Automatically works the same way.

delay.description: How long a transition that starts by itself waits after the slide's last step ends. It goes only beside `start: automatically`. Keynote's Delay works the same way.

duration.description: How long it takes. It's left out when the type is `none`.

direction.description: Which way a push, scroll, move in, reveal, or wipe travels across the screen.

color.description: The color of a fade through color: a color role, or a hex color written #RGB or #RRGGBB. A role takes its color from the scheme of the slide it leaves, and its alpha is ignored.

start.description: When it starts: on a click, or by itself after the slide's last step. The default is `on-click`. Keynote's Start Transition Automatically works the same way.

trim.description: The drawn part of a path's or a line's stroke.

start.description: Where the drawn part starts along the stroke in fractions of its length.

end.description: Where the drawn part ends along the stroke in fractions of its length.

utc-time.description: a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as "2026-10-17T19:30:00.000Z"

wipe.description: A reveal behind a moving straight edge. The defaults are progress 1, angle 90, and feather 0.

progress.description: How far the edge has crossed the object's box along `angle`. At 0, the edge is where the box begins. At 1, its soft edge is past the box's far side. A text's box includes the words that run past it.

angle.description: Which way the edge travels in degrees clockwise from up in the object's own axes. It turns and scales with the object and its groups, and a flip doesn't mirror it.

feather.description: How wide the soft edge is. It is in canvas units along the object's own axes and scales with the object. Across it, the object fades from shown to hidden.
